articles.title: Left-arm taking over: Zaheer Khan appointed as CSK head coach after Stephen Fleming's exit
articles.summary: Cricket News: NEW DELHI: Five-time Indian Premier League (IPL) champions Chennai Super Kings (CSK) on Monday appointed former India pacer Zaheer Khan as their head .
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Five-time Indian Premier League (IPL) champions Chennai Super Kings (CSK) on Monday appointed former India pacer Zaheer Khan as their head coach."Left Arm 'Taking' Over! Welcoming Zaheer Khan as the Head Coach of Chennai Super Kings," CSK said in a post on X.Zaheer Khan will take over as Chennai Super Kings' head coach from Stephen Fleming, who held the position from 2009 to 2026. CSK parted ways with Fleming after failing to make the play-offs for a third season in a row.Zaheer played 92 Tests, 200 ODIs and 17 T20Is for India. He was India's highest wicket-taker during their 2011 ODI World Cup-winning campaign, taking 21 wickets.Since retiring from the IPL in 2017, Zaheer has worked with several teams. He represented three IPL teams, Royal Challengers Bengaluru, Mumbai Indians and Delhi Capitals, before joining MI as their Director of Cricket Operations ahead of the 2019 season. He later became the franchise's head of global development.Zaheer was named Lucknow Super Giants' mentor for IPL 2025 but left the franchise ahead of the following season.As a player, Zaheer made 100 IPL appearances and took 102 wickets at an average of 27.27. articles.title: 'Pujara used to irritate us': Tim Paine recalls Australia's biggest headache against India
articles.summary: Cricket News: Puducherry: Former Australia Test captain Tim Paine is currently working with Australia A, who will take on India A in the first four-day game in Pudu.
articles.body: Puducherry: Former Australia Test captain Tim Paine is currently working with Australia A, who will take on India A in the first four-day game in Puducherry starting Tuesday. With Australia preparing for the next Border-Gavaskar Trophy (Jan-Mar 2027), Paine spoke to TOI about the importance of exposing young players to Indian conditions, the next generation of Australian bowlers and his memories of facing Cheteshwar Pujara and Rishabh Pant.How important are these ‘A’ tours for Australia?Very important. That’s why we’re investing quite a lot of time and resources into getting the next group of cricketers over here, whether it’s through Australia A, the MRF Foundation or some of the work we do with younger players. The Border-Gavaskar Trophy is a really important one for us. It’s been more than 20 years since we’ve won it in India. The more times we can get here, acclimatise to the weather, food and different batting and bowling conditions and develop game plans, the better.India A have players like Devdutt Padikkal and Sai Sudharsan. How do you see the contest?We want to see how our players adapt to them. There’s a lot of footage available, but if it was as simple as saying, ‘This is his weakness and this is how you get him out’, they wouldn’t be the player they are now. It’s an amazing experience for our young bowlers to bowl to players of that quality in these conditions.Which Indian batter was hardest to dismiss during your captaincy?(Cheteshwar) Pujara. He was hard to get out. He had great concentration and discipline and was tough. He used to irritate us. We were just trying to get him out. Pat Cummins eventually figured him out a bit and got him caught behind.How do you remember Rishabh Pant’s famous Gabba innings?I loved the way he came to Australia and played, how aggressive and confident he was. That’s something we’re trying to instil in this young group, the belief that you can go out and change games. That’s what Rishabh did against high-class bowlers. He threw them off their lines and lengths and put them under pressure. It was a great way to play, and a lot of the time I try and encourage our players to do the same thing.Are you surprised Pant is not part of India’s white-ball set-up?I haven’t watched enough of his white-ball cricket to say. I know his IPL over the last couple of years hasn’t been brilliant, but if he’s playing well, he could be playing in most white-ball teams around the world. It’s probably about capturing that form again and taking his red-ball cricket into white-ball cricket. There’s no reason why someone as skilled and talented as him, if he’s playing well, wouldn’t be a fantastic white-ball player.What are Australia’s chances in the next BGT?I think Australia have a good chance. Batting-wise, we probably haven’t scored as many runs as we would have liked in the last couple of summers, but there are still some high-quality players in the team. Either way, Australia will be very well prepared and I can’t see any reason why the Aussies can’t win.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'MS Dhoni obviously plays a key role': CSK reveal thinking behind Zaheer Khan appointment as coach
articles.summary: Cricket News: Chennai: Mahendra Singh Dhoni’s pinnacle as India captain was the 2011 World Cup triumph, and Zaheer Khan was one of that campaign’s unsung heroes. Hi.
articles.body: Chennai: Mahendra Singh Dhoni’s pinnacle as India captain was the 2011 World Cup triumph, and Zaheer Khan was one of that campaign’s unsung heroes. His joint-highest tally of 21 wickets in the tournament, alongside Pakistan skipper Shahid Afridi, and his opening spell of 5-3-6-1 in the final against Sri Lanka at the Wankhede are not celebrated as much as some of the other performances from that campaign.Now, as Dhoni enters the final chapter of his playing career, he has turned to his trusted lieutenant as coach of Chennai Super Kings, a team that has struggled to hit its customary heights over the last three seasons, failing to make the playoffs each time.After Stephen Fleming’s exit as CSK coach, there was considerable speculation over his successor. The management left the decision largely to Dhoni. Several names were discussed, including Hemang Badani, but one understands that the former captain’s comfort level with Zaheer was among the key factors behind the former left-arm pacer landing the job.Dhoni, as captain, had famously referred to Zaheer as the Sachin Tendulkar of bowling during India’s difficult 2012 World T20 campaign in Sri Lanka.“Dhoni obviously plays a key role in our decision-making process. He, along with captain Ruturaj Gaikwad and other members of the cricket committee, concluded that Zaheer is the best man for the job,” CSK managing director Kasi Viswanathan told TOI.CSK have struggled with their pace bowling lately, particularly at the death, and Zaheer’s mastery of reverse swing also worked in his favour.“Zaheer was a world-class bowler and has mentored many young cricketers, especially fast bowlers, over the years. As a player, he was one of the key reasons for India’s success during the 2000s,” Viswanathan added.Zaheer, on his part, said it was “an honour to be part of one of the most successful teams in the history of the IPL”.“As a cricketer, I have faced CSK on the field and thoroughly enjoyed those contests. I can’t wait to join this legacy franchise with such a rich history,” he said.The 47-year-old, who represented three IPL franchises (RCB, MI and DD) during his playing career, is no stranger to coaching.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Harmanpreet Kaur's India eye Asian Games gold repeat as they face Sri Lanka in final
articles.summary: Cricket News: Nagoya: In the almost three weeks of the Asian Games, the Indian women’s cricket team got a one-week window and three matches to win the title.With cr.
articles.body: Nagoya: In the almost three weeks of the Asian Games, the Indian women’s cricket team got a one-week window and three matches to win the title.With cricket still relatively unknown in the region, the players have been able to explore the city and its surroundings without attracting attention, from visiting the Shinto shrines and Buddhist temples of Kyoto, Japan’s cultural capital, to strolling through the streets of Nagoya. They have sampled local food, shopped and even found a taste of home at a Japanese-run Indian restaurant.At the Karogi Athletics Park cricket facility on the outskirts of the city, teams like Japan and Malaysia have rushed to meet India’s cricketers. For many of them, it’s a dream come true to meet icons like skipper Harmanpreet Kaur and Smriti Mandhana. The Indian diaspora, too, has come out in large numbers.Amid all the new experiences, they haven’t lost focus on the job at hand: to retain the gold.India hardly broke a sweat in the run-up to the final. However, Sri Lanka can be tricky customers, although India beat them in the Asia Cup less than two weeks ago.The battle for gold will be a repeat of the previous edition’s final, in which India got the better of the Lankans by 19 runs in a low-scoring final.That said, Sri Lanka have been in top form en route to the finale, registering wins against Malaysia and Pakistan. Skipper Chamari Athapaththu has led from the front with 146 runs from two matches, including two half-centuries. The 36-year-old cricketer is keen to make amends for the group-stage exit in the T20 World Cup and the Asia Cup runners-up finish.While the fancied Indians will settle for nothing but gold, the opposition is not being taken lightly.“Chamari is in good form. We know that she is one of their best players, so we have plans for her. That said, we will just try to execute our own plans,” opener Shafali Verma said.There’s a prediction of rain, so both teams will also have an eye on the weather. articles.title: Asian Games 2026: Pakistan women win bronze after beating Bangladesh by 31 runs
articles.summary: Cricket News: Pakistan women won the bronze medal at the Asian Games after beating Bangladesh by 31 runs in the third-place clash at the Korogi Sports Park on Tuesd.
articles.body: Pakistan women won the bronze medal at the Asian Games after beating Bangladesh by 31 runs in the third-place clash at the Korogi Sports Park on Tuesday.It was a strong all-round performance from Pakistan, who defended 145 after restricting Bangladesh to 114 in 20 overs.The win also helped Pakistan avenge their bronze-medal playoff defeat to Bangladesh at the 2023 Hangzhou Asian Games.Fatima Sana leads from the frontCaptain Fatima Sana once again played a key role for Pakistan.After Pakistan lost wickets regularly in the middle overs, Sana scored a crucial 45 off 30 balls to help her team post a competitive total.Gull Feroza also made a valuable contribution with 31 off 23 balls, while Aliya Riaz scored 25 off 22 deliveries.Bangladesh had earlier made a strong comeback with the ball. Nahida Akter, Shorna Akter and Ritu Moni picked up two wickets each as Pakistan slipped from 46/0 to 67/5.But Sana and Riaz changed the game with a 67-run partnership for the sixth wicket.The partnership helped Pakistan recover and finish on 145/8.Bangladesh lose early wicketsBangladesh's chase got off to a poor start as they lost three wickets for just 20 runs in 4.1 overs.Nigar Sultana and Sharmin Akhter then tried to rebuild the innings. The pair added 47 runs for the fourth wicket and gave Bangladesh some hope.However, the required run rate kept increasing.Nigar was eventually dismissed for 25 off 30 balls in the 14th over, leaving Bangladesh in deeper trouble.Sharmin remained unbeaten on 46 off 45 balls but struggled to find enough support from the other end.Umm-e-Hani seals Pakistan's winOff-spinner Umm-e-Hani was the star with the ball for Pakistan.She picked up three wickets for just 10 runs and played a key role in Bangladesh's collapse.Hani took two of Bangladesh's first three wickets, removing Juairiya Ferdous and Sobhana Mostary.After Nigar's dismissal, Bangladesh struggled to keep the scoreboard moving. Shorna Akter scored six, Ritu Moni three, Rabeya Khan four and Nahida Akter 10.Bangladesh eventually finished on 114 in 20 overs, falling 31 runs short of the target.Pakistan win third women's cricket medalThe bronze medal is Pakistan's third women's cricket medal at the Asian Games.Pakistan had previously won gold in the 2010 and 2014 editions.The victory also made amends for their defeat to Bangladesh in the bronze-medal match at the 2023 Hangzhou Asian Games.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Smriti Mandhana scripts history, becomes first woman to score 11,000 international runs
articles.summary: Cricket News: NEW DELHI: Smriti Mandhana added another landmark to her extraordinary career on Tuesday, becoming the first woman cricketer to complete 11,000 runs i.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Smriti Mandhana added another landmark to her extraordinary career on Tuesday, becoming the first woman cricketer to complete 11,000 runs in international cricket during India's Asian Games gold-medal final against Sri Lanka at Korogi Sports Park in Aichi-Nagoya.Mandhana entered the final needing just 13 runs to reach the landmark. She had accumulated 10,987 runs across Tests, ODIs and T20Is, with 788 in Tests, 5,411 in ODIs and 4,788 in T20Is. She wasted little time getting to the historic mark after India opted to bat first.The India vice-captain began with two boundaries in the opening over before launching a six in the third over to complete 11,000 international runs. The milestone added another chapter to a remarkable run of record-breaking performances for the left-hander.Mandhana had only recently taken the record for the most runs in women's international cricket across formats from former India captain Mithali Raj. She overtook Raj's tally of 10,868 runs with a spectacular 124 against Hong Kong in the Women's Asia Cup earlier this month, taking her total to 10,880 at the time.From Mithali Raj's record to 11,000-run landmarkThe 30-year-old has continued to rewrite the record books in the shortest format as well. During India's Asian Games semifinal against Bangladesh, Mandhana surpassed New Zealand great Suzie Bates to become the leading run-scorer in women's T20Is.She achieved the T20I milestone during her 37 off 19 balls in India's 114-run win over Bangladesh. At that point, Mandhana moved to 4,788 T20I runs, ahead of Bates' 4,758.Her latest landmark in the Asian Games final came just two weeks after she had established herself as the leading run-scorer in women's international cricket. Her 124 against Hong Kong was also her 18th international century, taking her past Meg Lanning and Laura Wolvaardt for the most hundreds in women's international cricket at the time.Mandhana's rapid accumulation of milestones has made the Asian Games a particularly memorable tournament for her. She also became the first Indian woman to hit 100 sixes in T20Is during the semifinal against Bangladesh.Mandhana, Shafali extend record partnershipMandhana also reached her half-century in the gold-medal clash off just 31 balls, continuing her aggressive start alongside Shafali Verma.The pair's latest stand further extended their record as the most prolific partnership in women's T20I cricket. Their aggregate partnership runs moved beyond 4,000, comfortably ahead of the UAE's Esha Oza and Theertha Satish, who are second on the list with 2,949 runs.Their partnership in the final also crossed another significant mark, with Mandhana and Shafali adding 99 runs against Sri Lanka on Tuesday.India entered the final unchanged after beating Japan by eight wickets in the quarterfinal and Bangladesh by 114 runs in the semifinal. Sri Lanka also retained the same XI after overcoming Malaysia and Pakistan to reach the gold-medal match. India's semifinal win was powered by Shafali's unbeaten 100 off 49 balls.The final is a rematch of the 2023 Asian Games gold-medal clash, as well as the Women's Asia Cup final earlier this month, both won by India. India are defending their Asian Games title after winning gold in their only previous appearance in the women's cricket event in 2023.Sri Lanka, meanwhile, are seeking their first Asian Games gold after winning bronze in 2014 and silver in 2022. Mandhana's 11,000-run milestone has added another historic subplot to the gold-medal showdown.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: Cricket News: New Delhi: Controversy has gripped the recently concluded season of the Delhi Premier League (DPL) with Vansh Bedi, who played for Central Delhi Kings.
articles.body: New Delhi: Controversy has gripped the recently concluded season of the Delhi Premier League (DPL) with Vansh Bedi, who played for Central Delhi Kings, reporting a "fixing approach" by a cricketer from a neighbouring state. It has learnt that the young wicketkeeper-batter flagged the approach to the Anti-Corruption Wing, which was later document as well."Vansh Bedi promptly reported a corrupt approach to the Anti-Corruption wing from a player from Uttar Pradesh, who was also playing a T20 league in the state. We have attached SLOs with every team this year and all our arrangements have been watertight," said the Delhi and District Cricket Association (DDCA) Secretary Ashok Sharma.The DDCA has written to the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) seeking advice on the matter, and how to approach the fixing claims stemming from a sting operation conducted by Tehelka."We have written to the BCCI and will await their guidance," added the DDCA secretary.It has also been learnt that, after being alerted by the DDCA, the Uttar Pradesh Cricket Association (UPCA) banned the Meerut Mavericks cricketer from playing in the UP T20 League.TimesofIndia.com has reached out to BCCI Secretary Devajit Saikia for a comment and the story will be updated the moment they respond. Insiders in the Delhi cricket corridors feel there is more than meets the eye but DDCA officials will act after receiving guidance from the Indian cricket board."DDCA would like to clarify that the allegations referred to in these reports are unverified and have not been established by any competent authority. The Association believes it would be inappropriate to draw conclusions about any individual, player or franchise based solely on such allegations," DDCA has said in a statement."Given the seriousness of the matter, DDCA has written to the respective authorities and shared the information that has come to its notice, requesting that the matter be examined through the appropriate established processes."Central Delhi Kings were the runners-up this season, losing to South Delhi Superstarz in the title clash. articles.title: 'Babar Azam struggles to handle captaincy': Waqar Younis warns 'we are losing a player'
articles.summary: Cricket News: Former Pakistan captain Waqar Younis believes the decision to hand Babar Azam the Test captaincy again could be hurting the batter's performances, arg.
articles.body: Former Pakistan captain Waqar Younis believes the decision to hand Babar Azam the Test captaincy again could be hurting the batter's performances, arguing that the team risks “losing a player” by placing the leadership burden on him.Waqar, who has served in several coaching roles with the Pakistan men's team, said Babar is a technically accomplished batter but appears to struggle when the additional responsibility of captaincy comes his way. He also suggested that Babar's inability to fully back his teammates under pressure makes the role unfair to both the players and the captain himself.“I have seen him as a player. Technically, a very sound player. Very complete and elegant player. As a player, I don't personally see anything wrong with him. But I think with the captaincy pressure, he takes a little too much on himself. Whenever he takes this responsibility or is given a responsibility, I don't think he performs that well,” said Waqar during an event.“So I think we are losing a player if we are going to give him this responsibility because he struggles to handle that. You have to be strong as a person, and you have to be really out there and back your players. If you cannot back your players, it's unfair to the players and the job,” he added.Waqar's remarks came shortly after Pakistan endured a 3-0 defeat against England in the three-Test series.The series was overshadowed by a major shake-up within the Pakistan camp. After Pakistan fell 0-2 behind, the Pakistan Cricket Board sent seven players and two coaches back home before the final Test.Babar also found himself at the centre of criticism after revealing ahead of the third Test that he had not been consulted by the board, headed by Mohsin Naqvi, over the decisions.The comment drew criticism from former Pakistan captain Wasim Akram, who questioned Babar for not standing by his team.Babar had returned to the Test captaincy earlier this year after Shan Masood was removed from the position following Pakistan's 2-0 series defeat against Bangladesh.Babar still waiting for Test centuryBabar's recent struggles with the bat have added another layer to the debate surrounding his leadership role.The 31-year-old has now gone almost four years without a Test century. His most recent hundred in the format came against New Zealand in December 2022.He came close to ending the drought against the West Indies and again in the third and final Test against England, but missed out on both occasions after being dismissed.Pakistan's recent results have also left them ninth in the World Test Championship standings with four points. articles.title: Smriti Mandhana, Richa Ghosh power India to highest-ever Asian Games total in gold-medal match vs Sri Lanka
articles.summary: Cricket News: NEW DELHI: Smriti Mandhana's blistering 79 and Richa Ghosh's explosive unbeaten 49 helped India post a daunting 216/3, their highest-ever total in wom.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Smriti Mandhana's blistering 79 and Richa Ghosh's explosive unbeaten 49 helped India post a daunting 216/3, their highest-ever total in women's cricket at the Asian Games, against Sri Lanka in the gold-medal match at the Korogi Sports Park on Tuesday.Batting first after Harmanpreet Kaur won the toss, India came out attacking from the outset, with Mandhana setting the tone in the opening over. The left-hander struck two boundaries off Sugandika Kumari before continuing her assault in the third over, smashing two successive sixes off the Sri Lankan bowler.Shafali Verma soon joined the party, and India raced to 40/0 after four overs. The fifth over, bowled by Sri Lanka captain Chamari Athapaththu, yielded 19 runs, including three sixes, as the opening pair took India to 59/0. India finished the powerplay at 67/0.Mandhana reached her 37th T20I half-century from 31 balls in the 10th over. The milestone was even more significant as she also became the first woman cricketer to complete 11,000 runs in international cricket.SCORECARD: India vs Sri Lanka, Asian Games gold-medal matchHowever, India lost Shafali later in the same over. Chamudi Praboda dismissed the opener for a brisk 48 off 29 balls, ending India's 99-run opening partnership. Shafali's innings featured three fours and three sixes.Mandhana lays foundation before Richa's late assaultMandhana continued to anchor India's innings as Harmanpreet joined her in the middle. The pair took India to 123/1 after 13 overs before Kavisha Dilhari ended their 42-run partnership by dismissing Harmanpreet for 19 off 17 balls.Richa then joined Mandhana and immediately maintained the tempo. The pair added 15 runs from Praboda's 16th over, taking India to 157/2.Sri Lanka finally got the prized wicket of Mandhana in the 17th over when Sugandika Kumari dismissed her for 79 off 45 balls. Mandhana's innings included five fours and seven sixes, leaving India at 163/3.There was no let-up in India's scoring after her departure. Richa took charge, smashing 14 runs from Kavya Kavindi's over as India crossed 180.The wicketkeeper-batter saved her most damaging assault for the final over. Taking on Mithali Ayodhya, Richa smashed 17 runs to propel India to 216/3 after 20 overs.Richa remained unbeaten on 49 off just 22 balls, with six fours and three sixes, narrowly missing a half-century but ensuring India finished with a formidable total.For Sri Lanka, Praboda, Dilhari and Kumari claimed one wicket apiece.The 216/3 surpassed India's previous best total in women's cricket at the Asian Games and gave the defending champions a substantial platform as they looked to retain the gold medal.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Shreyas Iyer enters history books, becomes first captain to do this in India-Japan 5-over T20I
articles.summary: Cricket News: Shreyas Iyer became the first captain from a Full Member side to elect to bat first in a five-overs-a-side T20I when India won the toss against Japan .
articles.body: Shreyas Iyer became the first captain from a Full Member side to elect to bat first in a five-overs-a-side T20I when India won the toss against Japan in the historic one-off contest at the Sano International Cricket Ground on Tuesday.The unusual decision came after rain and a wet outfield delayed the toss, originally scheduled for 9am IST, and forced the match to be reduced to five overs per side.With every ball carrying even greater significance in the shortened contest, Iyer opted to put India in to bat first, creating a unique statistical entry in T20I cricket.The match itself is a landmark occasion, with India facing Japan for the first time in men's T20I cricket. It is also part of celebrations marking 75 years of diplomatic relations between India and Japan. The game serves as the opening event of "Sport 75", an initiative designed to encourage sporting exchanges and greater cooperation between the two countries.India's first meeting with Japan adds another entry to an impressive record against new opposition.The Indian team have won 16 of their 19 matches in their first-ever meeting against an opponent. Their only defeats in such encounters came against New Zealand and West Indies, while their match against Scotland ended without a result.No other Full Member side has a better record than India in its inaugural meeting against a new opponent.India will be hoping that record remains intact in a contest that has been reduced dramatically because of the weather.India made a couple of notable selection calls for the shortened game. Vaibhav Sooryavanshi missed out once again, with Sanju Samson and Abhishek Sharma retaining their places at the top of the order. Both batters enter the match in outstanding form.Samson has struck back-to-back fifties, while Abhishek comes into the game after producing a stunning 30-ball century against Afghanistan. That hundred was the fastest T20I century by a batter from a Full Member nation.India have also opted to rest Jasprit Bumrah for the Japan encounter, with Yash Thakur coming into the playing XI.The match is India's only T20I before the men's team head to the Asian Games as defending champions, adding further significance to an already unusual contest.India (Playing XI): Sanju Samson(w), Abhishek Sharma, Ishan Kishan, Shreyas Iyer(c), Tilak Varma, Shivam Dube, Axar Patel, Washington Sundar, Yash Thakur, Ravi Bishnoi, Arshdeep SinghJapan (Playing XI): Lachlan Yamamoto-Lake, Reo Sakurano-Thomas, Kendel Kadowaki-Fleming(c), Benjamin Ito-Davis, Wataru Miyauchi, Alexander Shirai-Patmore(w), Charlie Hara-Hinze, Ibrahim Takahashi, Declan Suzuki-McComb, Makoto Taniyama, Shoma Sugaya-SlaterStay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: Cricket News: NEW DELHI: Shafali Verma continued her sensational run in T20I cricket in 2026, rewriting another record during India's Asian Games gold-medal clash a.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Shafali Verma continued her sensational run in T20I cricket in 2026, rewriting another record during India's Asian Games gold-medal clash against Sri Lanka on Tuesday.The India opener became the highest run-scorer in a calendar year in women's T20Is, surpassing South Africa's Laura Wolvaardt. Shafali's 29-ball 48 in the gold-medal match took her tally for the year to 863 runs, moving past Wolvaardt's 824.Shafali's innings at Korogi Sports Park featured three fours and three sixes and came at a strike rate of 165.52. Although she fell short of another half-century, her latest contribution extended a remarkable run in the shortest format.In 24 T20Is in 2026, Shafali has now scored 863 runs at an average of 39.22 and a strike rate of 162.83. articles.body: NEW DELHI: Harmanpreet Kaur-led side opened India's gold medal account at the Asian Games 2026 on Tuesday, defeating Sri Lanka in the women's cricket final at Korogi Sports Park in Nisshin to end the country's wait for a top-podium finish in Aichi-Nagoya.The defending champions produced a dominant performance in the gold-medal clash, first posting a mammoth 216/3 after opting to bat before bowling out Sri Lanka for just 69 to seal a commanding 147-run victory.The result gave India their first gold and seventh medal overall at the Asian Games, with the tally now standing at one gold, four silver and two bronze medals.Smriti Mandhana, Shafali Verma and Richa Ghosh were the architects of India's imposing total. Mandhana continued her assault and brought up her half-century before eventually falling for 79.Harmanpreet made 19, but Richa ensured there was no let-up in India's scoring rate. Her unbeaten cameo, which included six fours and three sixes, took India past the 200-run mark and set Sri Lanka a daunting target.With the ball, India maintained their dominance. Deepti Sharma (3/6) took three wickets, while fellow spinners Shafali Verma (2/3), Shreyanka Patil (2/9) and Shree Charani (2/13) claimed two wickets each as Sri Lanka were bowled out for a modest total.India join Pakistan with two Asian Games cricket goldsThe triumph means India now have two women's cricket gold medals at the Asian Games, having also won the women's cricket gold for the country in 2023.India had not participated when cricket featured at the Asian Games in 2010 and 2014. Their 2023 title and Tuesday's triumph now put them level with Pakistan, who won the women's cricket gold medals in 2010 and 2014.The men's competition will begin later in the Games, with the Shreyas Iyer-led Indian side scheduled to start their campaign in the second quarterfinal on September 28. articles.title: Lancashire cricket: What's gone wrong as Red Rose face unwanted history?
articles.summary: Lancashire are set to end 2026 in the bottom two of Division Two, their lowest-ever finish in the County Championship.
articles.body:
With one match of the 2026 season remaining, unwanted history beckons for Lancashire.

This proud county is staring at the lowest finish in their 136 years of competing in the Championship. They are seventh in Division Two and could finish bottom.

Never before have Lancashire ended a season either 17th or 18th position out of all the first-class counties, but after a miserable summer of red-ball cricket, it is now staring them in the face.

They begin the final round of games nine points above bottom side Gloucestershire, but it would be little surprise if Lancashire, who welcome runaway Division Two champions Durham starting on Thursday, were overtaken and ended up bottom of the pile given how the last few months have played out.

So how has it gone so wrong for one of English cricket's traditional powerhouses?

Since the launch of the two-tier system in 2000, Lancashire had previously spent only three years in Division Two, bouncing back to the top flight as champions at the first time of asking on each occasion.

But following a fourth relegation two years ago, things have been far from straightforward in the second tier.

Expecting a quick turnaround, head coach Dale Benkenstein left the club halfway through the 2025 season after Lancashire started with no wins from their opening seven Championship games.

By that point, captain Keaton Jennings had already resigned and an apology had been issued to members for poor results.

Just before his own departure, Benkenstein had talked about a lack of clarity , external within the club about whether the priority was to produce a winning team or to bring through young players. Fast forward over 12 months and that perceived issue has not been resolved.

Former player Steven Croft took over in an interim role from the South African and with three wins from the second half of the season with improved cricket and morale, he was handed the head coach job permanently.

With England legend James Anderson taking on the captaincy on a permanent basis for 2026, the hope was Lancashire would be challenging for promotion this year.

That certainly looked the case as the Red Rose won two and drew one of their first three matches, as Anderson took 21 wickets, including a match-winning 4-18 against Derbyshire.

However, a victory over Gloucestershire in Bristol was one that came at a heavy price as opener Luke Wells and new quick bowler Ajeet Singh Dale picked up injuries that turned out to be season-ending.

From that point in mid-April, the wheels have fallen off in a big way. Lancashire have proceeded to lose eight of the next 10 Championship matches, with the other two being rain-affected draws.

And it is in batting where the Red Rose's flaws have been primarily exposed.

Lancashire have posted one batting bonus point from the past nine matches - a total of 281-8 declared against Worcestershire in May - the only time a first innings score has ticked past 250.

Since the Championship resumed at the end of August, Lancashire's highest total in nine completed first and second innings is 192, with teenager Rocky Flintoff's 65 the highest individual score.

There have only been three Championship centuries all season and collapses have become commonplace, meaning the end-of-year batting averages are going to make for gruesome reading.

Take the last match against Kent. Openers Michael Jones and Jennings battled through the whole morning session on the opening day without losing a wicket, yet within 20 minutes of the restart after lunch, Lancashire had fallen from 81-0 to 82-4 and eventually lost all 10 wickets in the session to be all out for 161.

With the ball, no side has collected more bowling points than Lancashire, while Anderson and George Balderson are two of only six Division Two bowlers to take 50 wickets or more and the only ones in the same side.

But with not enough runs to play with, it has been hard to put opposition teams under serious and lasting pressure.

27 April: Durham (a) - LOST by eight wickets

10 May: Middlesex (h) - LOST by six wickets

18 May: Worcestershire (h) - Match drawn

21 June: Derbyshire (a) - LOST by nine wickets

23 August: Northants (h) - LOST by 316 runs

30 August: Worcestershire (a) - Match drawn

4 September: Middlesex (a) - LOST by 160 runs

11 September: Gloucestershire (h) - LOST by 105 runs

17 September: Kent (a) - LOST by seven wickets

Lancashire's title success in 2011 is their only sole Championship win since 1934, but that should not hide the fact that they remain one of English cricket's biggest teams, able to call upon far superior resources to most of the other sides in county cricket and certainly those in Division Two.

That only makes the paucity of current performances worse and the mood around Emirates Old Trafford is dark.

Many of the club's members are unhappy at how they believe cricket has been secondary in recent years to concerts and conferences and more attention diverted towards Manchester Super Giants in The Hundred.

Chief executive Daniel Gidney is stepping down, with Richard Kenyon arriving from Nottinghamshire to replace him while West Indies great Clive Lloyd has become the new club president and former captain and coach Mike Watkinson has been voted on to the board - with the hope of bringing cricketing expertise to fruition.

And significant change is set to happen this winter after Lancashire announced on Monday the departure of director of cricket performance Mark Chilton, the sign that things must improve on the field, with Gidney referencing the Championship as being at the heart of the club's 'cricketing vision' , external .

Remarkably, Lancashire have only won two red-ball matches in four seasons at Old Trafford and fans have watched their team be out-performed on home soil in all three disciplines by Northants and Gloucestershire recently.

Confidence in the team is low and head coach Croft knows it is a tough time for all concerned.

"You don't want to go through this as a player but usually you come out of it a better player," he told BBC Radio Lancashire after the three-day loss at Kent in the last round.

"Then you don't take it for granted when it is going well. But it's a horrible place to be in, as a team as a well as individuals, we're not really clicking.

"Four-day cricket is tough. It's a competitive division, some tricky surfaces, some of the lads have to problem-solve on the job, but that's what it's about to be a good four-day side."

Scott Read, BBC Radio Lancashire commentator

The numbers are well documented, and they don't make for pretty reading. Lancashire have not made 200 in any innings since June, their last batting point came in May and not since April have they managed to pick up more than two batting points.

Since their last win in April against Gloucestershire, they have lost eight of the following 10 Championship matches.

Lancashire have never finished bottom of the County Championship; it's a fate that they will probably avoid even though bottom club Gloucestershire have managed more wins heading into the final round of games.

It's the match against Gloucestershire in Bristol where things started to go wrong this year, season-ending injuries for Ajeet Singh Dale and Luke Wells in the same game deprived them of a new marquee signing and their opening batter.

In fact, they've used seven different opening partnerships this season, their first stand of 50 for the first wicket didn't come until September. Only two players have scored a century, Marcus Harris has done it twice with Paul Coughlin batting at eight being the other.

They've used 25 different players, it's been that kind of season.

Yes, the numbers don't make for pretty reading, at least those numbers don't. In the middle of all this is a remarkable display of endurance, fitness and sheer desire to play which has seen James Anderson miss only two red-ball games.

He's captained and carried the side all summer, ending the season with over 50 wickets. Not since 2005 has Anderson taken 50 wickets in a season for Lancashire. George Balderson has also passed 50 this year, the first time in his career he's reached that milestone.

The club continue to try to give younger players a chance - Rocky Flintoff, Arav Shetty, Joe Moores and Ben Walkden all featuring. But it's 15 years ago that Lancashire last won the title, it's over a decade since they last won major silverware.

And, since finishing second in Division One in 2022 the Red Rose have only won 11 of the following 55 Championship matches, with a relegation in 2024 and are now set for a third successive season in Division Two.

Cricket has a wonderful habit of making fools of us all, it can quickly prove us all wrong, but the trend is worrying and the fear among many members is that it may take some time to turn the fortunes of this famous old club around.

articles.title: Mark Wood: England fast bowler announces international retirement
articles.summary: England fast bowler Mark Wood announces his retirement from international cricket with immediate effect.
articles.body:
England fast bowler Mark Wood has announced his retirement from international cricket with immediate effect.

The 36-year-old, who is one of the fastest bowlers to ever play for England, has been blighted by injuries throughout his career.

The Durham paceman only returned to action in the first Ashes Test in Perth in November after 15 months out with an elbow injury followed by knee surgery.

However, he bowled just 11 overs before suffering swelling in the same left knee and subsequently flew home for treatment. He has not played for England since.

"Although this may not come as a surprise given the past year, it just feels like a natural time at the end of my contract," Wood said in a statement on social media.

"I've always tried to be resilient and come back from injury to prove people wrong and show everyone what I can do. Unfortunately, this time I lost the battle.

"On medical advice, Test cricket and 50-over cricket are not possible, so the England dream has slowly been ground out of me over the last year.

"Playing for England has been the greatest honour I could have ever wished for and a dream come true."

Wood added that he hopes to continue playing cricket in some capacity.

Wood took 119 wickets in 38 Tests after making his debut in 2015, and that summer he helped win back the Ashes on home soil.

However, he has suffered a string of ankle, knee and elbow injuries during his career.

In a bid to limit the stress on his body, he lengthened his run-up in 2018, and that did allow him to play key roles in some of England's biggest successes in recent years.

The altered run-up did not impact his pace and he was part of the team that lifted the 2019 50-over World Cup, where he took 18 wickets.

He was also in the squad that won the T20 World Cup in 2022, but missed the end stages of the tournament with a calf problem.

In white-ball cricket, Wood retires as England's sixth-highest wicket-taker in men's T20s with 54 from 38 matches, and he took 80 scalps in 70 one-day internationals.

Wood played a key role in helping England come from 2-0 down in the 2023 Ashes, with his return to the team - and blistering spells of bowling - helping them level the series.

"It's been a privilege to watch the latter part of a great career," said Rob Key, managing director of England men's cricket.

"To have been a point of difference in Ashes series wins, two World Cup wins, and to have thrilled crowds every time he got the ball in his hand is something very few players achieve. He can look back with enormous pride on a career very well spent."

'One of the most thrilling sights in the game'

Anyone who has ever played cricket at any level will have tried to bowl fast. The dream is to be able to hurtle the ball down at irresistible speed: batters flinching, stumps flying.

Mark Wood lived that dream. Few who have played for England, or any country, know what it is like to bowl with Wood's speed.

The sight of Wood flying in, bowling himself off his feet - literally, on many occasions - was one of the most thrilling in the game. He captured the imagination of supporters not only with his raw pace, but his personality. Wood engaged with supporters and never took himself too seriously. It seemed he always remembered that cricket is supposed to be fun.

Naturally, there will be the nagging doubt of what might have been had his career not been so badly hit by injuries. The human body is not designed to bowl fast and the rigours of the job hit Wood worse than most.

But, when the stars aligned, it was electrifying. A demolition of West Indies in St Lucia in 2019, complete with a remodelled, longer run-up, showed what Wood would be capable of in the latter part of his career.

He was one of the few England players to emerge with credit from the awful Ashes tour of 2021-22 and his entrance to the return series in 2023 was unforgettable.

Held back until the third Test, when England were already 2-0 down, Wood bowled at the speed of light at Headingley. In one of the great Ashes spells, Wood knocked over Usman Khawaja with a 95mph thunderbolt.

At the end of the Test, in a nail-biting run chase, Wood was at the crease with Chris Woakes to see England over the line. Woakes was another held back until the third Test and, without these great friends performing the way they did that summer, England would have been soundly beaten.

Wood has been a multi-format performer for England. He was in the XI on the unforgettable day at Lord's when the World Cup was won in 2019, coming out to bat with Ben Stokes despite carrying an injury. Wood was also in the squad when England lifted the T20 World Cup in 2022.

He is one of a handful of England players to have won both World Cups and the Ashes, having been part of the last England team to regain the urn in 2015. With Wood gone, the only remaining England player in Test cricket to have tasted Ashes glory is Joe Root.

There was no last hurrah in Australia. A long recovery from elbow and knee injuries did not produce the pace England were craving down under. Wood could only play in the first Test in Perth and said last month he was "ashamed" at what happened.

His retirement confirms the end of an era in English pace bowling. First Stuart Broad, then James Anderson, followed by Woakes and Wood into retirement. Throw in the all-round talent of Stokes, and England have lost 1,871 Test wickets in less than three years.

articles.title: Glamorgan Cricket: Colin Ingram to retire for coaching role at the club
articles.summary: Glamorgan's South Africa batter Colin Ingram is to retire aged 41 after 11 seasons with the county and will take up a coaching role at Sophia Gardens.
articles.body:
Glamorgan's South Africa batter Colin Ingram is to retire at the end of the season after 11 seasons with the county.

The 41-year-old says he will be taking on a coaching role with Glamorgan after 20 years of following his "dream of playing" and having "lived that every day".

Ingram is Glamorgan's longest-serving overseas player of the 21st century and was their top run-scorer in the Championship promotion-winning side in 2025.

He has scored 31 centuries for Glamorgan across the three formats with a career-best of 257 not out, and captained them in T20 cricket in 2018 and 2019.

Ingram made 40 international appearances in limited-overs matches for South Africa, where he represented Free State, Eastern Province and Warriors at domestic level, as well as playing part of the 2014 season for Somerset.

"Throughout my career I've dreamed big, worked hard, made memories, laughed and cried and seen things and places I never thought possible," he said.

"I've had a full crack and left it all out there."

Glamorgan's director of cricket Mark Wallace described Ingram as a "legend" of the club who has "had a lasting impact" on the county.

How new-look Glamorgan are preparing for pro level

The hard-hitting left-hand batter arrived at Sophia Gardens in 2015, quickly becoming a leading part of the team and a fan favourite.

He then played little Championship cricket for a five-year spell because of knee problems and T20 franchise commitments around the world.

Ingram featured in an impressive range of tournaments in Australia, India, Pakistan, the West Indies and the Middle East, as well as his native South Africa and the UK's Hundred competition, for Oval Invincibles.

Ingram, who returned to longer-form cricket in recent years after a successful knee operation, described cricket as his "art".

"I was fascinated by the game from a young age, and in particular batting," he said in a social media post announcing his retirement.

"At times, when it flows everything slows down and it feels like the most natural, instinctual thing I've ever done.

"Like my form of art and the bat my paint brush and it's exhilarating."

This season he scored centuries against Yorkshire and Warwickshire in the Championship and played a leading role in the home win over Surrey with 80 and 61 not out, but made only three limited-overs appearances.

He could return for a final farewell alongside fellow retiring stalwart Chris Cooke, 40, in the closing Championship match against Essex.

Ingram has an amazing county record of 5645 runs in first-class cricket averaging 47, plus 2630 runs at an average of 62 in one-day matches, and 3431 at 32 in T20 games.

He also took 67 wickets bowling leg-spin, mainly in limited-overs matches, and filled in as an occasional wicket-keeper.

On his future plans the South African said:

"As one chapter closes the next opens beyond the boundary as I begin my coaching career.

"My art is complete but I hope to influence the game positively and inspire players to be the best they can while enjoying their journeys."

Director of cricket Wallace said: "Colin Ingram is a Glamorgan legend. His performances, his leadership, and his character have had a lasting impact on this club.

"He has been central to our progress over the last 11 years, and his influence will continue through his new coaching role.

"We thank him for everything he has given to Glamorgan and look forward to seeing him shape the future of our playing group."

articles.title: Mark Wood: England fast bowler announces retirement from international cricket due to injury
articles.summary: England bowler Mark Wood talks exclusively to Sky Sports Cricket's Ian Ward about his decision to retire from international cricket due to a knee injury; Wood hasn't played since November 2025 and admits he rushed return from injury to play Ashes Test in Perth
articles.body:
Wood departs the sport having featured in 38 Test matches where he claimed 119 wickets.

The 36-year-old has not played for England since an eight-wicket defeat to Australia in the first Test of the 2025/26 Ashes series, where - in the series opener - he suffered a recurrence of the same injury which ruled him out of the remainder of the Ashes series.

In conversation with Sky Sports Cricket's Ian Ward on whether his decision to retire was difficult, straightforward or emotional, Wood replied: "Probably all of them. When you speak to other people, they say it hits you in the face, there's a big feeling around that being it: 'You're done.'

"I've never really had that, I love playing cricket, I love playing for England, that's been something I've felt really strongly about and proud to do. But I've had a lot of injuries.

"I've always found a way where I've believed I'd come back and had that resilience where I'm going to come back again, or I'll be better, or I'll prove somebody wrong again, but this time it's just ground me down really.

"I think it's been a long time since Perth, that was in November 2025 my last game, so it's been a year-and-a-half really where it's just sort of ground me down to thinking: 'I'm never going to get back to this level.'

"Plus the contract situation. My contract ends in September, and I think it just feels like the right time.

"I never really wanted to give up England, but the lads that are coming through are doing a fantastic job and the news should be about the lads going to get their contracts and I can just focus on other things."

Wood made his international debut in 2015 in limited-overs cricket, and retires having made 70 one-day international appearances and been a part of England's 50-over World Cup-winning squad in 2019.

He also played 38 T20 internationals and took nine wickets in four games as England won the World Cup in 2022, though injury would deny Wood the chance of playing in the semi-finals and final.

Wood will be part of the Sky Sports commentary team for Tuesday's one-day international between England and Sri Lanka in Durham.

2015: Left ankle injury, misses third Ashes Test

2016: Ankle problems continue, undergoes surgery and misses England's home Test summer

2019: Side strain, misses first two Ashes Tests

2022: Right elbow injury in the West Indies, requires surgery

2022: Body stiffness rules him out of the T20 World Cup semi-final and final

2024: Right thigh muscle injury against Sri Lanka

2024: Right elbow stress injury, ruled out for the remainder of the year

2025: Left knee ligament damage, undergoes surgery

2025-26 Ashes: Suffers recurrence of knee injury after returning to Test cricket

2026: Forced into international retirement after recurring knee problems

Wood: My knee never got right - I rushed back too quickly

Having expressed a determination to play for England again after his latest injury, Australia proved to be Wood's final Test appearance, ending a career beset and curtailed by injury.

"I knew it was bad [knee injury] because I'd had that previous surgery where I was always trying to chase my tail," Wood added to Sky Sports . "Looking back now, it probably never was quite right.

"I was always chasing that dream of, can I physically do this? My ankle problems, my elbow problems, all the rest of them, every time I went back, it felt better. This time, something wasn't quite right.

"Since I've had the second operation, things have improved, but not to the point where I believe I could play Test match cricket. I couldn't play 50-over cricket. I mean, I'd still love to play for England for 20 overs, but I think it just feels like a nice time to just say that's a natural end.

"Probably, from my point of view [came back too early and rushed return]. I don't think it's to blame anybody else, it was just, I was desperate to play Perth because it was the fastest wicket there.

"There and in Brisbane, they were the two games I was definitely trying to pencil myself in for.

"I hadn't had much time back on my legs. The warm-up game, my hamstring got incredibly tight because it was looking after my knee, and I think that whole time, when you talk about injury, people don't see the work you're putting in behind you.

"I was desperately trying to get it right. I was taped up to the nines, and I was like a mummy at one point I had that much tape on, but I just couldn't get back quite to that level, and I was just not quite the same in Australia."

articles.title: India script history, become first team to register 200 T20I wins after edging Japan in thriller
articles.summary: Cricket News: NEW DELHI: India scripted another milestone in their T20I history on Tuesday, becoming the first team to register 200 wins in men's T20 internationals.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India scripted another milestone in their T20I history on Tuesday, becoming the first team to register 200 wins in men's T20 internationals, including victories achieved through Super Overs.The landmark 200th win came in dramatic fashion as the world champions survived a major scare from hosts Japan, edging them by just two runs in a rain-shortened one-off T20I at Sano.With the match reduced to five overs per side because of rain, India posted only 32/4 after opting to bat. Japan came agonisingly close in the chase, finishing on 30/3 as India held their nerve to complete a historic victory.India's journey to 200 T20I wins began with their inaugural victory against South Africa in Johannesburg in 2006. They reached 50 wins against Sri Lanka in Colombo in 2017, completed 100 victories against West Indies in Kolkata in 2022 and reached 150 against Australia in Gros Islet in 2024.The latest victory against Japan took them into uncharted territory.India reach 200 wins faster than everIndia have now registered 200 wins from 291 T20Is, comfortably ahead of Pakistan, who have 174 wins from 299 matches. New Zealand are third with 137 wins from 267 matches, followed by South Africa with 131 from 235 and England with 130 from 233.India's progress through the 50-win milestones has also become increasingly rapid.They needed 83 matches for their first 50 wins, before taking 72 matches to move from 50 to 100. The next 50 came in 70 matches, while India required only 66 matches to move from 150 to 200 wins.The 200th victory, however, was far from routine.Axar, Washington help India survive Japan scareThe low-scoring contest was dominated by spin, with the damp surface and slow outfield making stroke-making difficult.Japan's spinners troubled India's star-studded batting line-up from the beginning. Charlie Hara Hinze dismissed Abhishek Sharma for a duck, while Ibrahim Takahashi accounted for Sanju Samson, who made 10. Benjamin Ito-Davis then removed Ishan Kishan for three.Skipper Shreyas Iyer top-scored with 16, but India could manage only 32/4 from their five overs, hitting just three boundaries.Japan looked capable of producing one of the biggest upsets in their cricketing history during the chase. Ravi Bishnoi conceded 10 runs in the third over, while Washington Sundar's penultimate over went for seven as Japan moved within striking distance.Washington finished with 2/13, while Axar Patel's experience proved crucial in the final over.Japan needed eight runs from the last six balls, but Axar gave Shirai Patmore and Benjamin Ito-Davis little room to attack. Rain had also left the outfield sluggish, making boundary-hitting even harder.There was late drama when a wide call against India in the final over was overturned after an appeal from Shreyas Iyer. articles.summary: Cricket News: England fast bowler Mark Wood announced his retirement from international cricket on Tuesday, ending an 11-year career after a long battle with injuri.
articles.body: England fast bowler Mark Wood announced his retirement from international cricket on Tuesday, ending an 11-year career after a long battle with injuries.The 36-year-old played 38 Tests, 70 ODIs and 38 T20Is for England, taking 253 wickets across all three formats.Wood last played for England in November last year during the first Test of the Ashes series against Australia. He bowled only 11 overs before suffering swelling in his left knee, the same knee on which he had undergone surgery the previous year. The injury ruled him out of the rest of the Ashes series, and he did not play for England again.In a post on social media, Wood said the decision came after medical advice and a difficult year with injuries."Although this may not come as a surprise given the past year, it just feels like a natural time at the end of my contract," Wood wrote.Wood has also dealt with ankle and elbow injuries during his career and said he had always tried to return stronger after setbacks."I've always tried to be resilient and come back from injury to prove people wrong and show everyone what I can do. Unfortunately, this time I lost the battle."He added that continuing in Test cricket and one-day internationals was no longer possible."On medical advice, test cricket and 50-over cricket are not possible, so the England dream has slowly been ground out of me over the last year."Wood made his Test debut in 2015 and was part of England's last Ashes-winning team, taking the wicket of Nathan Lyon at Trent Bridge to seal the series victory. He was also one of England's leading bowlers during the 2021-22 Ashes series in Australia, where he took 17 wickets.He played an important role in England's 2019 ODI World Cup-winning campaign at home, picking up 18 wickets in 10 matches. He was also part of England's T20 World Cup-winning squad in Australia in 2022."I got to live out a dream and I hope I can continue playing cricket in some capacity and pursuing other challenges in the future," Wood said.Wood finished with 119 wickets in 38 Tests, 80 wickets in 70 ODIs and 54 wickets in 38 T20Is. He took nine wickets during England's 2022 T20 World Cup-winning campaign, while his 18 wickets at the 2019 ODI World Cup came as England lifted the 50-over trophy for the first time.England men's managing director Rob Key paid tribute to Wood, saying the fast bowler "thrilled crowds every time he got the ball in his hand."Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Japan v India: Visitors avoid shock defeat after controversial wide is overturned
articles.summary: World Champions India avoid a shock defeat in the one-off T20 against Japan after a wide ball is controversially overturned in the final over.
articles.body:
India 32-4 (5 overs): Iyer 16 (12); Hara-Hinze 2-17

Japan 30-3 (5 overs): Kadowaki-Fleming 12 (12); Washington 2-13

World champions India avoided a shock defeat by Japan with a tense two-run win after a wide ball was controversially overturned in the final over.

In the one-off T20, which was reduced to five overs a side, Japan needed eight off the final over after their bowlers had remarkably restricted cricketing juggernauts India to 32-4.

Left-hander Alexander Shirai-Patmore was attempting to reverse-sweep spinner Axar Patel, who bowled the ball down the leg side - which would have been the batter's off side had he been attempting a conventional shot - and the umpire called it a wide.

After the umpire's signal, Axar was visibly frustrated with the decision and disputed the call alongside captain Shreyas Iyer.

The two umpires had a discussion after India's complaints and the decision was overturned, significantly taking the equation to six runs needed off three balls instead of five off four.

Axar then closed out the over to finish with figures of 0-7 off two overs and Japan finished agonisingly short on 30-3.

In white-ball cricket, any delivery bowled down the leg side is usually called a wide, but the ICC's playing conditions for men's T20 internationals state a batter loses those privileges from the moment he or she changes the position of their hands or feet to play a reversed shot.

In the conditions, it says a wide should be called "if the ball passes wide of where the striker is standing, and which also would have passed wide of the striker standing in a normal batting position".

This suggests the correct decision was reached eventually, but the incident has gained attention for how it was overturned despite there being no decision review system (DRS) in place for the match.

The preamble for the playing conditions also refers to the "spirit of cricket", with "accept the umpire's decision" listed as one of these points, although this is not one of the game's laws.

It was an agonising near-miss for Japan, who had struggled early on in their chase as they stuttered to 8-2 after two overs before taking 17 off the next two, which kept them in contention before the dramatic finale.

With the ball, they were led by 17-year-old spinner Charlie Hara-Hinze who took 2-17, including the wicket of destructive opener Abhishek Sharma first ball, before Shreyas' 16 off 12 balls provided some relief from his side being 14-3.

It was the first time the teams had played each other internationally because Japan have never reached a T20 World Cup, and the game was played in preparation for the men's Asian Games which start on 24 September.

Earlier, India cruised to victory in the women's Asian Games final as they thrashed Sri Lanka by 147 runs.

articles.title: India-Japan T20I wide controversy: What MCC laws say about umpire's reversal of decision
articles.summary: Cricket News: India survived a scare against Japan on Tuesday, edging the hosts by two runs in a rain-hit one-off T20 International that was reduced to five overs p.
articles.body: India survived a scare against Japan on Tuesday, edging the hosts by two runs in a rain-hit one-off T20 International that was reduced to five overs per side at the Sano International Cricket Stadium.Japan needed six runs from the last four balls while chasing India's 32 for 4. But the match took another turn when a wide call was reversed after protests from India.Left-handed batter Alexander Shirai-Patmore attempted a reverse-hit against Axar Patel and missed the ball, which went well down the leg side. The umpire called it a wide. The same sequence was repeated off the next delivery, with another wide called.The second wide decision was also initially given, but after Axar and India captain Shreyas Iyer protested, the umpire spoke to the leg umpire, New Zealand's Chris Brown, and reversed the decision.The equation then returned to six runs from three balls. Japan could score only three more runs and finished on 30 for 3, with India winning by two runs.The result gave India the record for the lowest total successfully defended in T20 cricket. It was also the first men's T20 meeting between India and Japan.India had struggled with the conditions after choosing to bat. The surface was sluggish and the outfield was slow, making it difficult for the batters to score freely. Iyer was the only Indian batter to reach double figures, scoring 16.What do the laws say?In white-ball cricket, a delivery that passes down the leg side is generally called a wide. The rule is intended to prevent negative bowling in limited-overs cricket.However, the rise of reverse sweeps and switch-hits has led to questions over how the rule should apply when a batter moves across and attempts such shots.The MCC's Law 22.4.1 says, "the umpire shall not adjudge a delivery as being a Wide, if the striker, by moving, either causes the ball to pass wide of him/her, as defined in 22.1.2 or brings the ball sufficiently within reach to be able to hit it by means of a normal cricket stroke."The laws do not specifically mention reverse sweeps or switch-hits, leaving some room for interpretation when a batter changes position and misses a delivery that would otherwise have been called wide.The MCC also sets out when an umpire can change a decision. Law 2.12 states: "An umpire may alter any decision provided that such alteration is made promptly and does not contradict Law 20.6 (Dead ball not to be revoked). This apart, an umpire’s decision, once made, is final."Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: ‘Disgraceful’: Did India bully umpires to win Japan T20 cricket match?
articles.summary: India survive a big scare against the hosts, beating them by two runs in a rain-hit T20 match in Sano, Japan.
articles.body:
It was the thinnest of margins, and a wide controversy.

Cricket world champions India are being accused of bullying the umpires in a Twenty20 match against minnows Japan, who came very close to scripting a major upset but fell short by two runs in a one-off encounter before the Asian Games.

Set a modest target of 33 by the three-time T20 world champions in a rain-curtailed match, Japan ended their innings on 30-3, handing India a two-run win at the Sano International Cricket Ground on Tuesday.

However, the match took a controversial turn in the final over as the hosts inched closer to the target.

What happened in the India vs Japan match?

India’s captain Shreyas Iyer won the toss after rain shortened the match to five overs per side. In T20 cricket, each innings is normally 20 overs long.

Japan made a dream start when Charlie Hara-Hinze had star Indian opener Abhishek Sharma caught in the first over. He then dismissed Ishan Kishan with the second ball of his second over to give the hosts hope of restricting India to a low total.

Iyer’s 12-ball 16 resurrected India’s innings as they finished on 32-4.

The hosts began their run chase on the slow and low-scoring wicket with caution. Slow left-arm bowler Axar Patel opened for India and dismissed Lachlan Yamamoto-Lake off his fourth delivery.

Japan needed 31 runs off the remaining four overs but lost another wicket while scoring six runs in the second, bowled by off-spinner Washington Sundar.

India continued bowling spin and conceded 17 runs in the next two overs but dismissed Japan’s captain Kendel Kadowaki-Fleming for 12 runs.

When Patel returned to bowl the final over, the hosts needed eight runs off it with seven wickets in hand. Following a dot ball and a single, Patel bowled a wide.

This left Alexander Shirai-Patmore on strike with Japan requiring six runs to win off four balls, and that is when the controversial moment arrived.

What was the wide controversy in the last over?

Patel’s next delivery was also signalled as a wide by the umpire. The batter attempted a reverse-sweep shot, but the ball was still out of his arc, so the wide was called.

However, India’s captain Iyer and Patel were furious with the call and remonstrated with the umpires. After a brief consultation, the umpires revoked the wide, denying the home side a run and an extra ball.

Japan scored three singles off the last three balls, leaving them two runs short of India’s total. Had the umpires not overturned the wide, Japan would have come closer to what would have been one of the biggest upsets in the history of international cricket.

Why are India being accused of bullying?

When umpires’ decisions are reviewed – either through a Decision Review System (DRS) call by the players or an umpire review when the on-field officials are unsure about a call – the ball in question is usually replayed on the screen and the TV umpire’s review is audible on broadcast and inside the stadium.

However, in this instance, the umpires did not call for a review and simply overturned the decision on the field, without offering an explanation.

Traditionally, players quarrelling with umpires publicly has also been frowned upon in the sport.

But the Indian captain and bowler showed no such restraint. Subsequently, the umpire overturned his decision without seeing any evidence that suggested he had been wrong in calling a wide.

Cricket journalists, experts and fans from across the world were quick to criticise the umpires.

Ben Gardner, cricket writer at Wisden magazine, termed it a disgraceful decision.

“With five off four needed for the biggest upset in cricket history, India have just bullied the umpires into overturning a wide call against Japan,” he wrote on X.

Others, like social media user Abu Zaid Sarooji, were even more blunt.

Even Indian cricket team supporters highlighted the controversy, saying it was clear that the batter did not change his stance before the ball was bowled and hence did not attempt to trick Patel.

What do the laws of cricket say about revoking a wide?

According to law number 22.3, which pertains to the revoking of a wide ball call in the Marylebone Cricket Club’s Laws of Cricket, an umpire can revoke a wide ball if:

There is then any contact between the ball and the striker’s bat or person before the ball comes into contact with any fielder.

However, neither of the above was applicable in this case.

The on-field umpires were Chris Brown of New Zealand and Chris Thurgate of Japan. Thurgate was the umpire at the bowler’s end and made the initial call to declare the ball a wide. After Iyer and Patel protested, Thurgate and Brown consulted with each other, before the decision was reversed.

Did the captains talk about the incident after the match?

Neither captain broached the topic, but the Japanese players looked gloomy and disappointed as they walked back after the match.

“Honestly speaking, it was a very difficult wicket to bat on,” Iyer said. “A five-over game, ‌‌it can go anywhere. It doesn’t matter how good a team you are.”

“The attitude and approach the Japanese team showed today was impeccable, and kudos to them. Their approach was outstanding. I’m sure that they are on the right track.”

Why did Japan host a T20 match against India?

According to reports, the match was a result of diplomatic manoeuvring, corporate sponsorship and years of quiet groundwork by the Japan Cricket Association (JCA), which has been helping the sport ⁠⁠take root in the country.

The JCA pulled off a major coup when it persuaded India to play the home side, the Reuters news agency said earlier this month.

The JCA had been working for more than a year to persuade its Indian counterpart, the BCCI, to play a T20 International in Sano. Those efforts gained momentum in recent months when the Japanese government ⁠⁠got involved.

“One match or competition itself won’t change anything, and we are certainly not going to think that suddenly it’s going to be as popular as baseball or football in Japan,” JCA chief executive ‌‌Naoki Alex Miyaji told Reuters.

“But the match against India is the first page of a new era.”

Kadowaki-Fleming said he was extremely proud of his team’s ‌‌performance against such formidable opposition.

“Emotions are running pretty high in our group. But the fact that we’re able to run the best team in the world, in my opinion, to the last ball of ‌‌a ‌‌game is pretty special,” he said. “I think today was a really momentous occasion in that it was the first time we were able to face a full member.”

Was this Japan’s most high-profile cricket match?

It was the first time that Japan, an associate member of the International Cricket Council (ICC), faced a full member and that too a top T20 side.

Japan are 41st in the ICC T20 men’s rankings, while the women’s team is ranked 39th.

Japan has only 7,300 registered players and 16 cricket grounds.

articles.title: England beat Sri Lanka by 89 runs after Will Jacks heroics in one-day international in Durham
articles.summary: Will Jacks stars as England comfortably defend 266 to take 1-0 lead in ODI series against Sri Lanka; watch the second ODI live on Thursday from 12pm live on Sky Sports Cricket (first ball 12.30pm)
articles.body:
Will Jacks starred with bat and ball, hitting an handy 46 not out off 47 balls before completing a career-best 5-22 to wrap up the Sri Lankan tail.

Captain Harry Brook (67 off 69 balls) top-scored after electing to bat at the toss but a middle order wobble inspired by debutant Sachindu Colombage (3-44) restricted England to 265 in 48.1 overs.

England took steady wickets to hamper Sri Lanka's pursuit of 266 before Jacks struck three times in the final over as the tourists were bowled out for 176 in 37 overs.

England take ODI series lead over Sri Lanka

England's decision to bat first after winning the toss was immediately tested when Tom Banton fell to a jaffa from Asitha Fernando, the delivery nipping back to clip the bail on top of off stump.

The hosts weathered the early setback, with Joe Root sharing 50-run partnerships with Ben Duckett and Harry Brook to steer England to 135-2 after Duckett was trapped lbw by Dunith Wellalage.

Root's 68-run stand with Brook was ended when he was deceived and bowled by the mystery spin of debutant Colombage, six runs short of his half-century.

The dismissal of England captain Brook, caught off the bowling of Dushmantha Chameera after reaching a seventh ODI century in 49 balls, sparked a middle-order collapse.

Jos Buttler was trapped lbw before Rehan Ahmed was run out by a superb direct hit from Charith Asalanka. Jamie Overton, Gus Atkinson and Jofra Archer were then all bowled by Colombage, Dilshan Madushanka and Fernando respectively, as England lost six wickets for 65 runs in 15.5 overs.

Will Jacks led England's resistance with an unbeaten 46 from 47 balls, including an explosive 18 in the 48th over as the hosts moved beyond 250. But the late charge was cut short when Fernando produced a reverse-swinging yorker to clean up Josh Tongue.

Sri Lanka negotiated the first five overs of their chase of 266 without alarm before Kamindu Mendis holed out to Duckett at short midwicket off Atkinson.

Tongue then accounted for Sri Lanka's other opener, inducing an edge through to wicketkeeper Buttler as the tourists slipped to 51-2.

Banton produced a stunning, sharp catch at extra cover to dismiss the driving Pavan Rathnayake, before Jacks trapped a sweeping Asalanka lbw three balls later to leave Sri Lanka 85-4 and in deep trouble.

Overton struck again three overs later, tempting Janith Liyanage into a loose waft outside off as he edged behind to leave Sri Lanka 100-5.

The writing was on the wall when captain Kusal Mendis was trapped lbw by Jacks, leaving Sri Lanka reeling at 105-6. Their woes deepened when Colombage suffered the same fate against Rehan Ahmed.

Wellalage led a brief Sri Lanka fightback, plundering 17 from an Ahmed over before his 42-run partnership with Chameera revived hopes at 133-7.

But Jacks extinguished those hopes in a decisive final over, removing Wellalage, Fernando and Madushanka to wrap up the victory.

Player of the match Will Jacks (46no off 47) and 5-22 in 7 overs:

"It was a really good all-round performance from the team there.

"I am getting used to this role now. It is more about playing the situation and playing what is out there.

"Having batted on it and what it was like, I knew I was going to play a decent role.

"No matter the time, you have got to do your best."

"It wasn't the easiest of surfaces but we want to be a team that can adapt to conditions. We did that well today.

"We knew exactly what we were going to do with the ball out there and we did that beautifully.

"I think the clarity we went out into the field with was outstanding. We communicated very well."

articles.body: NEW DELHI: Delhi wicketkeeper-batter Vansh Bedi has denied any connection with the controversy surrounding a sting operation that alleged the misuse of confidential team information in Indian cricket, saying attempts to link him to the case are "false and defamatory".Bedi, who was part of the Chennai Super Kings (CSK) set-up during IPL 2025 and later played for Central Delhi Kings in the Delhi Premier League (DPL), broke his silence on Tuesday after his name began circulating on social media following an undercover investigation involving former domestic cricketer Rachit Bhatia.In a statement posted on Instagram, Bedi said he was not the unnamed CSK player mentioned during the sting operation and had no involvement in the allegations made by Bhatia.“I categorically state that I am not the individual referred to by Ex-Ranji Trophy cricketer Rachit Bhatia in the sting operation concerning alleged match-fixing involving a CSK player, nor do I have any involvement whatsoever in any such activity,” Bedi wrote.He also said that any attempt to connect him with the allegations was defamatory and that his legal team had started the process of taking action.Bedi said his lawyers were pursuing “appropriate civil and criminal action” against those responsible for circulating the claims.The original undercover investigation did not identify Bedi as the player who allegedly supplied confidential information to Bhatia. However, his name later began circulating online.Earlier on Tuesday, the Delhi & District Cricket Association (DDCA) also responded to media reports about alleged corruption in the Delhi Premier League, calling the allegations "unverified".“DDCA would like to clarify that the allegations referred to in these reports are unverified and have not been established by any competent authority. The Association believes it would be inappropriate to draw conclusions about any individual, player or franchise based solely on such allegations,” the DDCA said in a statement.“Given the seriousness of the matter, DDCA has written to the respective authorities and shared the information that has come to its notice, requesting that the matter be examined through the appropriate established processes.”Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates.
